events.title: VPEG formed as a Missouri limited partnership.

accounts.label: Jan. 2010
accounts.text: The JLP complaint says the Fund was formed in January 2010.

events.title: First investors join, described as “family and friends.”

accounts.label: Late 2010 or early 2011
accounts.text: The court describes the first investors as family and friends, joining in late 2010 or early 2011.

events.title: Last independent audit, according to the JLP complaint.

accounts.text: Alleged: no independent audit since 2011.

events.title: The Oliver plaintiffs invest about $11 million.

accounts.text: Decided to invest after a 2017 presentation.
Initial investments made from 2018 to 2023.

accounts.label: “Not long after” 2010
accounts.text: Invested “not long after” the Fund's 2010 launch.

events.title: The Fund buys a $320,000 note-and-warrant unit in Victory Energy.

accounts.label: Feb. 3, 2017
accounts.text: A 12% six-month promissory note plus a warrant for 5,203,252 shares at $0.0923, paid from the Fund's working capital.

events.title: SEC filing: Zamber and Cosby sign as managers of the general partner.

accounts.label: Feb. 28, 2017
accounts.text: The Fund, Visionary PE GP I, LLC, Zamber and Cosby file jointly. Zamber and Cosby are described as the managers of the general partner and the managing directors of the Fund. Zamber reports 36.5% of Victory's stock.

accounts.label: Mar. 16, 2026 (the court's conclusion)
accounts.text: The court concluded Zamber and Cosby are the sole members of the general partner.

events.note: Two sources, nine years apart, describe the same control structure. The later date is when the court said it, not when it began.

events.title: The Fund lends to Victory on a secured convertible note.

accounts.label: Aug. 21, 2017
accounts.text: Victory reports a secured convertible original-issue-discount note with the Fund.

events.title: Form D: a $25 million offering, with nothing sold yet.

accounts.label: Jan. 26, 2018
accounts.text: The Fund notifies the SEC of a $25,000,000 equity offering under Rule 506(b). It reports $0 sold, the first sale “yet to occur,” no investors yet, and no non-accredited investors. Signed by Zamber as Managing Director.

events.note: The court record has investors joining from late 2010, and about $90 million raised by the time of the 2025 hearing. A Form D can cover one new offering, and this one does not say whether earlier sales happened under other offerings. EDGAR shows no amendment reporting later sales.

events.title: The managing director's view of the bank account is cut off for long periods.

accounts.label: 2018 on
accounts.text: Testimony: access was cut off for long periods starting in 2018; the account is managed by Zamber and Cosby, and wires need both signatures.

events.title: Victory settles the first note in stock and borrows $2 million more from the Fund.

accounts.label: Apr. 10, 2018
accounts.text: $1,410,200 of debt is satisfied for 1,880,267 shares and a warrant. The Fund then lends $2,000,000 on a new note with a 10% original issue discount.

events.title: The Victory loan is raised to $4 million in three steps.
At least one distribution to limited partners.

accounts.text: At least one distribution was made. Its amount and recipients are unclear.

events.title: Wires of $50,000 and $175,000 go to Zamber, three days apart.

accounts.label: Aug. 13 & 16, 2021
accounts.text: Testimony describing two wires from the Fund's account.

events.title: A text asks for “a wire for $270k (deferred compensation) today if possible.”

accounts.label: Oct. 19, 2021
accounts.text: A text message quoted in the JLP complaint.

events.title: South Bend meeting: “no debt at the Fund level.”

accounts.label: Sept. 2022
accounts.text: Alleged statement that there was no debt at the Fund level, and that a distribution was coming.

events.title: Investors lend $1.6 million on promises of a quick sale of portfolio companies.

accounts.text: Short-term loans of $1.6 million from plaintiffs, plus $100,000 from Hart, on assurances of monetization “within three to six months.” None repaid by June 2025.

events.title: Trustee board meeting: a distribution “right around the corner.”

accounts.label: Mar. 2023
accounts.text: Alleged statement at a trustee board meeting.

events.title: A May 2023 “harvest season” presentation.

accounts.label: May 2023
accounts.text: Alleged investor presentation.

events.title: JLP Partners subscribes for $100,000.

accounts.label: May 12, 2023
accounts.text: The later class plaintiff's own investment.

events.title: Victory owes the Fund $3,815,926.

accounts.label: June 30, 2023
accounts.text: Balance described as “including principal and accrued interest,” though the same filing says the notes bear no interest beyond the original issue discount.

events.title: Victory merges with H2EG; the Fund's loan becomes stock.

accounts.label: Dec. 1, 2023
accounts.text: The Fund's note converts at $0.075914 into 7,866,034 shares plus 43,095,923 prefunded warrants. Zamber and Grenley leave Victory's board. H2EG holders end up with about 81%.

events.title: Victory's filing calls Kevin DeLeon a “General Partner” of the Fund.

accounts.label: Dec. 4, 2023
accounts.text: DeLeon, Victory's CEO, is described as a “General Partner and Director of Corporate Strategy” of the Fund. Grenley is described as Director of Capital Development, with the Fund since 2012.

accounts.label: June 4, 2025 (as summarized)
accounts.text: DeLeon, for Highgate Capital, LLC, denied signing papers identifying LLC membership.

events.note: A title in a portfolio company's filing is not the same as membership in Visionary PE GP I, LLC. The two statements are about different questions, and neither settles the other.

events.title: Unaudited statements: $218,000 cash and a net loss over $10 million.

accounts.label: End of 2023
accounts.text: Statements marked “unaudited, unreconciled, and non-tax basis.”

events.title: Executive summary reports $5.8 million in distributions.

accounts.label: Mar. 1, 2024
accounts.text: The defendants' own summary.

events.title: Updated report shows $9.1 million in distributions.

accounts.label: July 23, 2024
accounts.text: The updated report, as described by the court.

accounts.label: June 2024
accounts.text: The same report, dated June 2024.

events.note: Same kind of figure, two editions: $9.1 million minus $5.8 million is $3.3 million.

events.title: A summary from Cosby shows year-to-date gross profit of $14.50.

accounts.label: Sept. 30, 2024
accounts.text: Testimony about a summary document.

events.title: A lien filing names the Fund as debtor.

accounts.label: Nov. 12, 2024
accounts.text: Alleged lien over all assets.

accounts.label: Nov. 2024
accounts.text: A lender's UCC filing appears; the same day, a text asks for a “10k wire to RZ.”

events.title: Most recent rent payment as of the April hearing.

accounts.label: Dec. 30, 2024
accounts.text: Testimony at the April 28, 2025 hearing.

events.title: Court lets the receiver sell some Circle stock and borrow from plaintiffs.

accounts.label: Jan. 13, 2026
accounts.text: Up to $265,000 of Circle Internet Group stock may be sold, only at $82 a share or more. A $275,000 unsecured loan from plaintiffs is approved, for a $540,000 fund used for the 2024 and 2025 required minimum distributions. The court holds it keeps supervising the receivership despite the appeal.

events.title: Three defense motions denied; the fraud claims go ahead.
